To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
JNK3 silences insulin gene expression and protects beta-cells mainly through maintaining a normal IRS2-to-Akt2 signaling pathway.

(1) the brain/islet-specific JNK3 isoform is required for normal expression of IRS2 in beta-cells, (2) JNK3 silences the pro-apoptotic FoxO3A transcription factor, and (3) JNK3 maintains the activity of Akt2 and GSK3β in insulin-secre ting cells.

JNK1/ JNK2 and JNK3 have opposite effects on the Akt signaling pathway and that JNK3 protects insulin-secreting beta cells from apoptosis and dysfunction through the maintenance of a normal insulin-signaling pathway.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the regulation of beta-cell function and survival by the stress-responsive JNKs.
the role of JNK3 in insulin-secreating cells.
the role of JNK3 in regulating beta-cell function and survival, and the mechanisms by which it exerts its effects.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
JNK1 and JNK2 are pro-apoptotic, while JNK3 is anti-apoptotic.
the three JNK isoforms have opposite effects in beta-cells, and that JNK1 and JNK2 are mainly cytoplasmic pro-apoptotic factors while JNK3 is mainly nuclear anti-apoptotic factor.
JNK3 is a key regulator of beta-cell survival and function, while JNK2 is a regulator of beta-cell apoptosis and dysfunction.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the JNK3 isoform is a key player in maintaining the normal function of the pancreatic beta-cells.
JNK1 and JNK3 are pro-apoptotic and anti-apoptotic respectively in beta-cells, while JNK2 seems to be pro-apoptotic in the cytoplasmus, but anti-apoptotic in a nuclear compartment.
JNK3 is a pro-survival factor for beta-cells, and that JNK1 and JNK2 have opposite effects on beta-cell survival.
The main takeaway from our work is that
JNK1 and JNK2 have opposite effects to JNK3 on insulin secretion, and that the balance between these JNKs is important for the regulation of beta-cell function and survival.
JNK3 may be considered as an attractive target for the treatment of type 1 diabetes.
the three individual JNKs are differentially involved in the regulation of insulin-signaling and beta-cell apoptosis.
